channel.description: WSJ World News RSS, without Opinions

item.title: Spain’s Second High-Speed Train Crash This Year Leaves Dozens Dead
item.description: At least 68 people were killed when two trains collided south of Madrid.

item.title: U.K. Budget Keeps Government on Track to Stay Within Rules
item.description: The U.K. government set out new plans for spending and taxation intended to keep it on track to narrow its budget deficit, but at a slower pace than previously hoped for.

item.title: Netanyahu, Israel’s Divisive Political Houdini, Is Still at the Center of the Show
item.description: The prime minister may still falter. But he topped the polls despite an all-out effort to bring him down.

item.title: Arab States Must Invest in Productive Sectors After Iran War Exposes Weaknesses, U.N. Official Says
item.description: EXCLUSIVE: The war shock has hastened the need to move away from the Gulf states’ rentier economies, Abdallah Al Dardari said.

item.title: Bolsonaro Lands in Miami After Fleeing Brazil
item.description: The defeated presidential candidate faces two criminal investigations in his home country, which had canceled his passports.

item.title: Oil Prices Rise as Houthi Militants Target Saudi Energy
item.description: The Houthis said Tuesday that they struck Saudi Arabia’s Ras Tanura refinery in the Eastern Province with a ballistic missile.

item.title: German Consumers Grow Slightly Gloomier on Lingering Inflation Concerns
item.description: The country’s consumer-climate index fell to minus 30.8 in its forecast for November, from minus 30.6 in October.

item.title: Best High-Yield Savings Accounts of October 2026: Up to 5.00%
item.description: Beat average interest rates with one of these top high-yield savings accounts.

item.title: Israel Braces for Uncertainty With Early Election Results Pointing to Deadlock
item.description: With more than three-quarters of the votes counted, Benjamin Netanyahu’s coalition was in the lead but remained shy of the 61 seats needed to form a government.

item.title: U.S. Warns Gulf of Possible Short, Intense Renewal of Iran War After Midterms
item.description: There are new signs that the American and Israeli militaries are preparing a potential wave of strikes to muscle Tehran to the negotiating table.

item.title: China’s Electric Carmakers Are Running Out of Domestic Buyers
item.description: Plus, Netanyahu faces a high-stakes showdown over whether he will stay in office, and the brutal Harvard class everyone wants to take.

item.title: Netanyahu Holds on as Election Results Show No Clear Winner
item.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s results improved as votes rolled in, but was shy of a majority and short of the seats his coalition currently holds.

item.title: U.S. to Issue Visa for Brazil’s Flávio Bolsonaro as Questions Swirl About His Location
item.description: Brazil canceled Bolsonaro’s passports after he defied a Supreme Court order to turn over the documents, a Brazilian official said.

item.title: Overseas Handler Linked to Iran Behind Foiled RAF Air Base Attack
item.description: Mohmed Ahmad Abdulkarim was charged with assisting a foreign intelligence service, which police believe to be Iran.

item.title: Global Soccer Star Kylian Mbappé Just Apologized to China—for a Mao Zedong Meme
item.description: The striker was dropped by Chinese sponsors after laughing at an image of his face on the former Chinese leader’s body and referring to him as a “dictator.”

item.title: Oil Futures Fall as Market Holds Out Hope for Middle East Diplomacy
item.description: Oil prices fell, with U.S. benchmark crude slipping back under $100 a barrel as traders held out hopes for regional diplomatic efforts to ease Middle East tensions.

item.title: China Claims Strong Economic Growth, but Skeptics Question Official Figures
item.description: Beijing has reported robust growth this year, but a growing chorus of economists are asking if the numbers are accurate.

item.title: We Went to Cuba to See How the Fuel Crisis Is Forcing Havana to Open Its Economy
item.description: Watch to learn why escalating sanctions and a fuel blockade haven’t toppled Cuba’s regime but are transforming its economy.

item.title: U.K. Fiscal Discipline in Focus Ahead of Burnham Government’s First Budget
item.description: Investors will be watching for a possible increase in the bank corporation tax surcharge, higher taxes on gambling, and changes to property taxes.

item.title: Xi Wants to Play Peacemaker. Trump Has Other Ideas for a Historic Summit.
item.description: Plus, Xinjiang goes from blacklisted to global trade hub, Xi’s purges echo Stalin’s, and Kim Jong Un makes a surprise trip to China.
